Observed:
- Intractable vomiting
- Postprandial upper abdominal pain
- Marked gastric distension
- Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and the aorta
- 1-week history of intractable vomiting
- Bloating
- Compliant with fasting customs
- Markedly lean
- Progressive inability to tolerate oral intake
- Dehydrated and exhausted on examination
- Abdominal ultrasonography and plain radiographs showed marked gastric distension
- Nasogastric tube placed for decompression
- Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed compression of the third portion of the duodenum
- Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy was normal
- No intrinsic luminal lesions found on endoscopy
Differential diagnosis:
1. Superior Mesenteric Artery Syndrome
2. Gastric Outlet Obstruction
3. Duodenal Stenosis
4. Small Bowel Obstruction
5. Median Arcuate Ligament Syndrome
